- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast.  
- If model consistently forecasts below true price for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” bias: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with recent upward momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5+), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing out extreme swings; use 3-period moving average for stabilization.  
- If true price drops sharply after a model peak, model often fails to recognize “reversal” — adjust downward by 2–4% in next 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
